findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods above 41F.
1) FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs sitting at an ambient temperature of 58F.
2) TCS foods in the kitchen prep cooler (including but not limited to raw hamburger, cut tomatoes, shredded lettuce, and cheese) to have internal temperatures between 56-59F.
The PIC verified the eggs and items in the prep cooler had been out since 8 AM (2 hours).  CORRECTED- items were moved under TIME AS CONTROL- to be used or discarded with a total of 4 hours (by 2PM). When items are unable to maintain temperature control (below 41F or above 135F) they must be used or discarded within 4 hours. Ensure all  temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F, OR marked to be used or discarded within 4 hours after removing from temperature control to limit the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the kitchen prep cooler (nearest the dish machine) to be failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F. The PIC stated the unit will be serviced or replaced. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/20 to verify compliance. Contact the inspector sooner if the problem is resolved.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed single service to-go containers with the food contact surface facing upwards at the server station. CORRECTED- the containers were flipped. Ensure food contact surfaces are inverted or placed under covering to protect from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the inner gaskets of the double door cooler (at the kitchen’s entry) to be significantly frayed. Discussed with the PIC. Replace by the next routine inspection to prevent potential contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed an electrical outlet below the kitchen microwave to be lacking plate covers. Place covers on these outlets to prevent the entry of food or other debris, which may enter the wall. Physical facilities should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment:
Multiple incidents of bare hand contact were observed during today’s inspection:
1) The salad tongs at the server station were in contact with the food.
2) The ice scoop was in contact with the ice in the ice machine.
3) A bowl was stored as a scoop in tomato sauce in the walk in cooler. 
CORRECTED- the tongs and ice scoop were moved so that the handle was no longer in contact with the ready to eat (RTE) foods. The bowl was removed from the tomato sauce. Ensure scoops (that have handles) and tongs are stored in such a manner to prevent bare hand contamination. Improper hygiene practices are one of the top five risk factors for food borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 2 cans of tomato sauce on the bottom of the can storage rack to contain dents within the body and along the seam. CORRECTED- The inspector pointed out the dents to the person in charge (PIC), who stated they will be removed the cans from service to be returned to supplier (currently the cans above create a weight that make them inaccessible). Remind employees to check cans for dents along the seams to prevent the entry and growth of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ground beef (minimal internal temperature of 155F) stored above whole cuts of beef (minimal internal temperature of 145F). CORRECTED- the ground beef was moved below the whole cuts and education regarding surface area contaminants for ground products was provided. Inspector provided the PIC with a storage order handout. Ensure all animal proteins are stored by increasing internal cooking temperatures to prevent contamination of foods with lower (-no) cooking temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket near the kitchen entry to have soap, and no measurable concentration of chemical sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket (Chlorine bleach) was remade to 100 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at a frequency to hold the sanitizing concentration of food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm for Chlorine bleach). Do not use soap for chemical sanitation, as the soap and sanitizer combined decrease each product’s intended use.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs sitting at an ambient temperature of 86 on wire shelving in the kitchen. The PIC verified the eggs had been out since 10 AM (3.75 hours). CORRECTED- the eggs were discarded. Ensure all  temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F, OR marked to be used or discarded within 4 hours after removing from temperature control to limit the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Date marking was absent from nearly all TCS food items through the facility. Items include, but are not limited to: cut tomatoes, cut potatoes, fish, and other animal proteins. CORRECTED- dates or preparation were placed on TCS foods. Ensure all TCS foods are labeled with the date of preparation/ thawing/ opening, to be used or discarded within SEVEN days. The day of preparation/ thawing/ opening counts as day ONE.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a gap in the back door along the bottom and left perimeter, allowing light to enter. This gap may serve as a location for pest to enter the facility. Ensure weather stripping is placed to seal the gap by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed edible taco bowls stored (inverted) on top of the double door cooler nearest to dish machine. CORRECTED- the taco bowls were covered. Ensure all food is stored in a manner to protect from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet sanitizer cloth stored on top of single use butter and jams near the kitchen door. CORRECTED- the wet sanitizer cloth was moved to the sanitizer bucket. Ensure all wet sanitizing cloths are stored in a chemical sanitizing solution to prevent the harborage and spread of pathogens with a high water activity.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was present at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a CFPM arrived shortly after the inspection began. Inspector gave literature to the person in charge (PIC) that contains different ANSI-approved institutes which offer CFPM courses. Inspectors suggest more staff obtain their CFPM to ensure a CFPM is present at ALL TIMES food is being prepared or served.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed an employee use their bare hands to turn off the faucet after hand washing. CORRECTED- inspector provided education regarding the need to use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet (and prevent recontaminating freshly cleaned hands). Review proper hand washing techniques with all staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a sanitizer bucket to be made in the kitchen hand washing sink. CORRECTED- inspector reminded PIC to use the facility’s triple sink to make sanitizer buckets. Hand washing sinks should be used for hand washing only, so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces in the facility in need of cleaning:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The fans in the walk in cooler contain a significant amount of dust. 
2) The fans in the double door cooler next to the dish machine contain an accumulation of dust.
3) The handles of the double door cooler next to the dish machine contain a significant amount of food debris.
4) There was a significant amount of grease accumulated in the space between the grill and the grill coolers.
5) A significant amount of food splash was observed on the wall behind the cook line.

Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, grease, and other debris. These debris poses a risk to contaminate ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order: 

(1) The raw beef stored over various ready-to-eat foods in the double cooler to the left of the cookline (near the dish machine). During the inspection the raw beef was moved onto a bottom shelf. 

(2) Multiple containers of raw chicken stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler. During the inspection the raw chicken was moved onto a bottom shelf. The facility stores all raw meat in the back left corner of the walk-in cooler and the inspector suggests labeling the bottom shelf for chicken storage only. 

Ensure that raw foods are stored below ready-to eat-foods and raw meats are stored according to internal cooking temperatures. Due to the amount of repeat violations the health educator will be reaching out to schedule food storage education at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed the prep cooler on the cookline is currently not functioning. The PIC was aware that the cooler was not functioning and prior to the inspection implemented a time-as-control (TAC) policy for temperature control for safety foods inside the cooler (cut tomatoes, lettuce, mayo, and cheese). The majority of the foods had already been removed from the cooler and only condiments and cut vegetables were being stored in the top. While they had implemented a TAC policy they were not writing down the time when food must be discarded. The PIC was aware of the time the foods were put into the cooler and during the inspection a note pad was brought to the prep table and the foods in temperature control were recorded. The PIC stated that a new part has already been ordered to fix the cooler, but until it is serviced they will continue to use TAC. The inspector will follow-up on 7/10/2025 to check on either the TAC procedure or that the cooler is properly functioning. Ensure that foods are properly marked to indicate the four hour TAC window until the cooler is cold holding foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a sandwich stored on a dry wiping cloth on the prep table during the inspection. The cloth is absorbent and not a smooth, easily cleanable surface. The PIC stated that the employees set the sandwich down on the wiping cloth while they were finishing the plate. The sandwich was removed and the PIC was educated to store food in another location. Ensure that food is always stored on a food contact surface that can be sanitized before and after use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket on the cookline was stored adjacent to the steam table. Stored in this position the sanitzier bucket presents the risk of contamination from splashes. The PIC was educated and the bucket was moved during the inspection. Ensure that toxic materials are stored in a position where they do not pose the risk of contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: (1) The grease drips forming over the hood system; and (2) The food debris, grease, and soil accumulating on the table surface underneath the grill holding clean dishes. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris, grease, and other soils. Ensure that the hood system and table surface under the grill are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there are two large holes on the wall to the left of the ice machine. The holes are from a hanging object on the wall being recently moved. The holes must be sealed (ex.caulked) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that both of the PIC’s allergen awareness certificates are expired and no one else present at the facility when the inspector arrived had completed the training. The PIC was reminded that all CFPM (certified food protection managers) must obtain basic training in allergen awareness principles. During the inspection an employee with the allergen training arrived at the facility. Ensure that the facility is in compliance with allergen training requirements by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the ground outside the grease dumpster has an accumulation of grease. The PIC was instructed to deep clean the area. They were also reminded that grease must be dumped carefully to avoid large spills onto the ground. Employees began the process of cleaning the spill during the inspection using cleaning chemicals, water, and scrapers. The inspector will return on 11/25/2024 to ensure that it has been sufficiently cleaned and has remained clean.

5-501.111: Storage areas, enclosures, and receptacles for REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be maintained in good repair and clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee pour bleach into a sanitizer bucket and then continue preparing food on the cook line without washing hands and changing gloves in-between. After a discussion the employee washed their hands and changed gloves. The inspector instructed the PIC to educate staff about washing hands after any activity that may have contaminated hands. Ensure that employees clean hands before engaging in food prep and after potential contamination. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed an employee filling up a bucket in the hand washing sink. The inspector educated the employee and the PIC that hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. The employee proceeded to fill up the bucket in a different sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any purpose other than hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the following foods stored in positions that presented the risk of contamination: (1) Eggs stored over cooked noodles in the walk-in cooler (REPEAT VIOLATION); (2) Various raw meats stored over cooked rice in the walk-in cooler; (3) Uncovered sausage and ham in the walk-in cooler; (4) Eggs stored over cheese in the kitchen prep cooler bottom (REPEAT VIOLATION); and (5) Raw beef stored over hot dogs in the left double cooler (next to the single freezer) on the cook line. The foods stored in incorrect positions were corrected and uncovered foods were covered during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that raw meats must always be stored below ready-to-eat foods. The PIC was also given an educational handout which the inspector suggested hanging on cooler doors. Ensure that foods are always protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer buckets in the kitchen were testing at 10 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. The PIC was educated about testing and routinely changing sanitizer buckets. A capful of bleach was added to each bucket during the inspection. After the sanitizer buckets were testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are always testing between 100-200 ppm (Cl). Also ensure that test strips are used regularly to test concentrations and that buckets are changed as needed. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed single service utensils at the front counter stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. The inspector educated about storing food contact surfaces in the same direction so that employee only touch handles The storage order was corrected during the inspection. Ensure that utensils are always stored with the food contact surfaces in the same direction to prevent contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the gasket of the two-door standing cooler on the left side of the cook line (next to the single freezer) is in disrepair. The gasket is becoming de-attached from the door. Physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. Ensure the gasket is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed the facility did not have employee health reporting forms. The PIC was provided with blank copies during the inspection. Ensure that all employees sign the reporting forms and they are kept at the facility. There will be a follow-up on 08/29/2024 to check that all employee health reporting forms have been signed.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed employees using bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods. Bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods observed during the inspection included: using bare hand to hold a head of lettuce while cutting, using bare hands to put the two pieces of sandwich bread together, and bare handing pickles and tomatoes while putting them on a sandwich. The PIC was asked to throw away the products which were handled with bare hands. The inspector educated the PIC about always using a barrier while handling ready-to-eat foods. The inspectors asked the PIC to find gloves to leave on the sandwich prep line for handling ready-to-eat foods. The PIC found some gloves and the employees working the sandwich prep line put on the gloves during the inspection. The PIC was instructed to ensure that employees are always wearing gloves when handling ready-to-eat foods. 

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a hand washing sign at the hand sink in the kitchen. There always needs to be a handwashing sign notifying employees they must wash hands before returning to work. The PIC was provided with a handwashing sign during the inspection which was posted by the hand sink.

6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
This is a repeat violation: Observed a container of tooth picks stored directly in the pickle container along the sandwich prep line. This container was removed, wiped down with a sanitizer rag, and placed in a location that does not pose a health hazard. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, and display. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed eggs being stored over ready-to-eat foods (including, but not limited too, cheese and pineapple) in the walk-in cooler and bottom of the sandwich prep cooler. Foods must be protected from cross contamination during storage. The eggs were moved below the ready-to-eat foods during the inspection. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed tongs being stored on the handle of oven doors. When the oven doors are opened, it presents the risk of contamination if the tongs touch the ground. The tongs were moved from this position and placed by the triple sink to be cleaned. The PIC was instructed to store the tongs in a new location.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
This is repeat violation: Observed the single service utensils at the front counter to be stored with the handles and mouth portions of the utensils intermingled. Front area PIC will be ensuring this correction is made to have all the single service items facing the same direction. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed there is a build-up of ice on the fans in the walk-in freezer. The build-up of ice is not a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have an accumulation of food debris/soils that are in need of being cleaned: (1) Build-up under the filters in the coffee machines; (2) The shelves holding clean dishes by the dish machine; and (3) The shelves holding spices above the mixing station to the right of the hand sink. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the floors of the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer (including under the shelves) have an accumulation of soil, debris, and food spills. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the gaskets of the two-door standing cooler by the cook line are in disrepair. The gaskets are not attached to the door in some locations. Make sure that the gaskets are repaired or replaced to ensure that physical facilities remain in good repair.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
